channel.title: Chain Times
channel.description: Chain Times reports crypto news: bitcoin and ether markets, exchanges, DeFi protocols, stablecoins, regulation, security incidents and network upgrades.

item.title: What Is a Multi-Hop Route, and How Does It Work?
item.description: A multi hop route in crypto swaps sends tokens through intermediate pools, such as A to ETH to B, when deeper liquidity can improve your output.

item.title: When Is a Solana Priority Fee Needed for Busy Accounts?
item.description: A Solana priority fee is an optional per-compute-unit charge that helps transactions land when the network or touched accounts are busy; quiet transfers need none.

item.title: DeFi transaction reversals and on-chain finality
item.description: Can a DeFi transaction be reversed by support? No after confirmation. Learn why finality matters, what you can replace while pending, and what to do next.

item.title: How to Back Up a Seed Phrase Before Your First Withdrawal
item.description: Back up your seed phrase before moving crypto off an exchange: write it offline, restore the wallet, match its address and test a small withdrawal first.

item.title: How ERC-4626 vault share price grows over time: Interest and fees
item.description: An ERC-4626 vault share price grows over time when interest raises totalAssets faster than fee shares expand totalSupply, lifting each share’s value.

item.title: Base’s Challenge Period Explains Why Withdrawals Wait
item.description: A challenge period in optimistic rollups gives anyone seven days to dispute a Base state claim; withdrawals finalize on Ethereum only if the claim stands.

item.title: EU proposal targets crypto networks in Russia sanctions package
item.description: The European Commission has proposed targeting crypto and payment networks in its 22nd Russia sanctions package, which still needs approval from all 27 EU states.

item.title: BTC swap API integration: bridge and vault routes compared
item.description: TeleSwap vs THORChain API: THORChain routes BTC to native assets; TeleSwap mints teleBTC on EVM and can swap it, giving app developers two distinct integration paths.

item.title: Yapı Kredi uses Ripple custody tech for crypto platform
item.description: Yapı Kredi is using Ripple’s custody system for its crypto platform, adding bank-based asset safeguarding as Türkiye requires platforms to use authorised custodians.

item.title: EU proposal targets Russian banks and crypto networks
item.description: The European Commission proposed targeting 60 Russian banks and crypto networks in a new sanctions package, with measures that need approval from all 27 EU states.

item.title: Low-liquidity swaps: start tight, reduce size before widening
item.description: What slippage tolerance should you use for a low-liquidity token swap? Start tight, then widen only as needed—or cut the trade size or compare pools.

item.title: Staking GNO on Gnosis Chain: validator or pool
item.description: Yes, you can stake GNO after bridging it to Gnosis Chain: deposit 1 GNO per validator or use a liquid pool; set a withdrawal address you control.

item.title: Stableswap pools: Why balance changes the price
item.description: What is a stableswap pool in DeFi? It keeps trades near 1:1 for balanced pegged assets, then raises price impact as the pool becomes imbalanced.

item.title: Which gas setting should you use for a bridge transaction?
item.description: Low vs market vs aggressive gas settings for bridging: choose Market by default, Low when the network is quiet and time allows, or Aggressive near a deadline.

item.title: What Is Slippage Tolerance? Set a Swap Limit That Fits
item.description: Slippage tolerance in crypto swaps is the largest drop from the quoted output you’ll accept before the trade cancels; it sets your minimum received.

item.title: Spreadsheet vs crypto tax software: software suits complex DEX trades
item.description: Spreadsheet vs crypto tax software for recording DEX trades: software fits frequent swaps and LP activity; a spreadsheet suits a few dozen simple trades.

item.title: EU proposes crypto crackdown in 22nd Russia sanctions package
item.description: The European Commission has proposed targeting crypto and payment networks linked to Russia, aiming to curb sanctions evasion in its 22nd sanctions package.

item.title: EU proposal targets Russian banks and crypto networks
item.description: The European Commission proposed targeting 60 Russian banks and crypto networks in a new sanctions package, but all 27 EU states must approve it.

item.title: EVM Compatibility: What Carries Across Chains
item.description: What does EVM compatible mean for a blockchain? It means Ethereum contracts, wallets and addresses can work across chains that run the Ethereum Virtual Machine.

item.title: DEX router contract: What happens in a swap
item.description: A router contract in a DEX swap takes your tokens, routes them through pools, checks the minimum output and sends you the result—or reverts in one transaction.
